text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to read, not to add new features. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller parts, or remove duplicated logic. While the external behavior stays the same, the quality of the code improves significantly. This practice helps reduce technical debt, which is the hidden cost of messy or rushed work. By regularly refactoring, you make future changes faster and safer, since clear code is simpler to understand, test, and modify.
